record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; no experiment outputs or source code were read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README uses a projected-out refusal direction as part of its NSKI safety method and reports the method's summary performance. It does not report a test of the original causal claim; this is a repository/tool description, not a replication with reported experimental artifacts.
record.gate_note: The README reports an NSKI-versus-baseline summary table. It does not tie the table to a model, benchmark, judge, or experimental configuration. The listed Arditi and Belitsky comparison values are not results of the direction intervention itself. Experiment scripts and result directories are listed, but that does not establish that they ran or that their results support the README table.
record.test_reason: The README presents NSKI, a KV-cache intervention built on a harmful-minus-harmless direction, and reports only its own method's summary performance. No model, dataset, judge or setup is tied to the table. This is a tool's own-method result, not a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The README claims NSKI reaches 5% ASR at 100% utility with O(1) cost, beating a 46% baseline and the Arditi (15%) and Belitsky (18%) comparisons. None of these figures is tied to a stated model, benchmark or judge.
record.recipe_differences: The README says it extracts a harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation difference and projects the direction out, but applies the projection to value representations at a target attention layer rather than reporting the original all-layer, all-position residual-stream intervention. Repository type: tool/implementation; no replication results are documented in the README.

fits_no_version.finding: The README claims that projecting a harmful-minus-harmless direction out of value vectors at one attention layer lowers ASR from 46% to 5%, with 100% utility. No model or setup is given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Projecting the refusal direction from KV-cache values acts as a safety defense (lower ASR). This is unverified and runs opposite to the V1 ablation prediction.

record.problems: The README gives only summary percentages, without identifying the evaluated model, tying results to datasets or judges, giving uncertainty, or providing verifiable experiment outputs in the supplied file list.
record.rows_left_out: The README's Arditi et al. and Belitsky et al. comparison values are omitted because they are results for other methods, not the direction-removal intervention itself. The listed experiment scripts and result/figure directories have no reported outcomes in the supplied text.

untested.parts: All parts: ablating or adding the direction and its effect on refusal rates, plus capability preservation, for an identified model.
An adversarial.py experiment is listed in the structure, but no results are reported.
Multiple supported models are listed, but no transfer result is reported.

record.verdict_notes: This is a repository README only, with no results files reported. Its claim that removing the refusal direction reduces ASR is mechanistically odd relative to V1, but it is unanchored. It should not count as a challenge.

versions.untested_parts: The README describes projecting the extracted direction from value representations at a target attention layer, not the claimed residual-stream ablation at every layer and position; it does not establish whether removal causes compliance or whether general capabilities are broadly preserved.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration result is reported.
No reported test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
No test of affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
No separate harmfulness-judgment and refusal-decision measurement.
No reported cross-language, cross-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer result.
No comparison of refusal training methods or timing.
